correctness.rationale: For every n>=3, each selected incidence constrains two adjacent oriented cycle edges to a common sign. Nonconstant cyclic orientations are acyclic and admit a total vertex order. Thus a marked 0,+,- word is a face precisely when adjacent nonzeros never disagree and a single-sign word has an adjacent zero pair. For a fixed simplex the augmented signed trace is -(-1)^c where c is the number of permutation cycles on selected incidences. For rotations of period d=gcd(n,a), weighted signed words give -tr[T(-1)^d]+2tr[U(-1)^d]=-1+6[3|d]-4[4|d], with d=1,2 addressed directly. Reflections swap the sign and force boundary sites/pairs zero; the j free mirrored pairs give Z_0=1,Z_1=-1,Z_{j+2}=-Z_j and the three stated parity cases. Finite-group transfer on barycentric subdivisions then yields the two quotient reduced Euler averages and mod-24 periodicity. Independent enumeration from acyclic edge orientations (not the submitted verifier) reconstructed all faces and 84 dihedral signed actions for n=3..9, agreeing exactly. The symbolic orientation/transfer proof, not finite tests, establishes all n.
residual_risks: No individual Betti groups, nonreduced quotient homotopy, integrality of separate homology representations, or torsion is established.
Finite independent actions n=3..9 corroborate rather than prove the all-n theorem; independent reasoning verifies the transfer identities and acyclic orientation extension.

The invariant is the complete virtual D_n-action and its two natural quotient reduced Euler characteristics for every n, supplying nonidentity rotation and reflection symmetry information unavailable from ordinary face counts or the known pure-subcomplex character. The 24-periodic quotient formulas constrain proposed equivariant decompositions even without a full Betti census. This is a motivated all-parameter structural result, not an arbitrary narrow numerical recomputation.
residual_risks: This only classifies alternating rational character, not all graded rational representations or torsion.
